explanation: A regularized logistic model on character n-grams is a strong, robust first real baseline for high-dimensional sparse text and directly addresses the dummy model's chance-level evidence. The balanced class weight matches the nearly even class counts, while the char analyzer can capture subword and morphological patterns without relying on external tools or test data. This experiment is preferable before deeper XGBoost variants because it is simpler and gives clearer evidence about whether the text representation carries signal.
diagnosis: Only a dummy baseline has been evaluated, scoring 0.5117 accuracy on a balanced two-class text dataset. This is effectively chance-level and provides no evidence that any text signal has been learned; there are no repeated model failures yet, so no failure-driven switch is warranted.
next_action: Train and validate the logistic regression candidate with C=1.0, char analyzer, separate representation, and balanced class weights as the first non-dummy text model, then compare its accuracy against the dummy baseline.
abandoned_strategy: Dummy/constant baseline, because it only establishes chance-level performance and cannot exploit text features.
